A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEC-based identification framework and PQAL algorithm. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and semi-synthetic dSprites experiments, including prediction errors, effective-rank measurements, and acquisition-strategy comparisons in Table 1 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds semi-synthetic IHDP and ACS Folktables evaluations in Table 1, with settings in Appendix E.3.

M1.justification: The two-stage kernel estimation, CME-uncertainty acquisition, bridge-adaptation objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged in Section 5 and Algorithm 1. Renaming the conditional expectation operator from E to T does not change the method.

E1.justification: Section 6.1 adds semi-synthetic IHDP clinical data and ACS Folktables socioeconomic data to the retained synthetic and dSprites coverage. These introduce infant populations partitioned by birth weight and geographic populations partitioned by US state, while generating latent confounders, proxies, and outcomes synthetically.

E2.justification: Existing comparator membership is unchanged, including SC appearing only for Dataset 2 in Table 1. IHDP and Folktables reuse FewShot_ERM, Proxy-DA, and Oracle. The acquisition comparison retains random selection, Z-uncertainty, and the EER-inspired RPX strategy.

E3.justification: The added benchmarks introduce standardized sinusoidal or cosine proxies, mean-projected covariates, noisy synthetic outcomes, and specified target Beta-mean shift profiles. Appendix E.3 describes their two-source, 60-query evaluations. Settings for the retained experiments, including source sample counts and query allocation, are unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing shift-robustness analysis is extended to IHDP and Folktables, testing prediction as target latent means move toward the lower tail. The proxy-imperfection/effective-rank analysis and acquisition-strategy ablation remain unchanged; their new diagnostic interpretation does not constitute another experiment.

E5.justification: Existing seed counts and Figure 4's 95% confidence-interval reporting are retained. The added benchmarks use six seeds, matching the existing dSprites practice. Table 1 continues to report point estimates without uncertainty, and no new statistical estimation or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 preserves all original scores and substantially extends the results with five shift levels for each added benchmark. At degree 5, PQAL versus Proxy-DA MSE is 0.067 versus 0.110 on IHDP and 0.132 versus 0.150 on Folktables. PQAL leads the non-oracle methods at IHDP levels 2–5 and all Folktables levels. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and Appendix A.2 revise the mathematical comparison with completeness. v1 directly argues that completeness implies the full-rank condition; v2 replaces that step with an argument about injectivity on LEC-constant functions and qualifies the theorem accordingly. The other identification proofs and acquisition guarantee are substantively retained.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces querying a 'minimal set' of domains with a 'small, targeted set', narrowing the minimality claim. The abstract and introduction extend the stated empirical coverage to IHDP and Folktables. The central LEC, point-identification, and PQAL contributions remain.

C2.justification: New Remark 2 substantially expands interpretation and verifiability of compatibility, proxy spanning, and integrability, linking observable CME rank to assumption diagnostics. New Section 8 explains failure under uninformative proxies, rank-deficient environments, outcome variation hidden within LECs, and changing causal mechanisms. This materially expands the discussion of applicability beyond v1's formal conditions.

D1.justification: Equations 20–21 and Appendix E.3 add construction details for the new benchmarks, including proxy normalization, covariate projection, birth-weight and state assignments, Beta parameters, and query budgets. No code or hardware disclosure changes. The new Beta lists contain an ambiguously printed entry, (1,5,5), limiting exact reproducibility.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ding et al. (2021), Ruth et al. (2024), and Louizos et al. (2017) for the new datasets and semi-synthetic evaluation rationale. Remark 2 more explicitly relates the assumptions to already-cited proximal-inference work. Section 7's principal research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 expands the background and assumption explanations, adds a Discussion section before the conclusion, and locally revises the experimental narrative. Operator notation and author affiliations also change. Most prose and the overall organization, including the appendix structure, remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains IHDP and Folktables blocks while retaining its columns and visual format. The existing figure graphics and captions are unchanged, although figure placement relative to surrounding text shifts as the document reflows. There is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added clinical and socioeconomic evaluations broaden the empirical evidence, while Remark 2 and Section 8 make the assumptions and failure conditions easier to assess. The reduced minimality claim also improves calibration. The gain remains limited: the added outcomes and proxies are synthetic, Table 1 still lacks uncertainty estimates, and an ambiguous Beta parameter weakens reproducibility of the new settings.
